name: Sweet Basil
summary: A warm-season branching basil with the same structural logic as Genovese: early pinching, repeated stem harvests, and flower removal when leaf production is the goal.

germination.guidance: Sweet basil commonly germinates in about 5–10 days under warm seed-starting conditions.

thinning.short: Thin by crowding, not by a universal one-seedling rule
thinning.guidance: In a compact pod, keep the strongest stems and remove crowding when leaves begin to overlap heavily or stems compete for the same light path.

pruning.short: Pinch above a healthy node to branch
pruning.guidance: Treat Sweet Basil like other branching basils: remove the growing tip above a healthy leaf pair once established, then repeat light cuts as branches develop.

harvest.short: Harvest stems while preserving active nodes
harvest.guidance: Regular outer-leaf and stem harvest supports continued production; leave enough foliage and active nodes for rapid recovery.

flowering.guidance: Ferry-Morse recommends removing flower buds to encourage fuller, leafier growth when culinary leaves are the priority.

hydroponics.short: Use the same basil family guardrails, then validate the actual system
hydroponics.guidance: Basil is a proven hydroponic crop, but Garden should keep system-specific pH/EC recommendations tied to the hydroponic source layer rather than the seed packet.

problems.short: Watch flowering, crowding and weak elongated stems
problems.guidance: Future AI Check should combine canopy shape and history instead of diagnosing from age alone.

name: Curled Chervil
summary: A cool-season delicate herb that prefers moist conditions and bolts in heat. It is better managed by light leaf harvest than by structural pruning.

germination.guidance: Johnny's recommends barely covering chervil seed because light supports germination; expected emergence is about 10–14 days.

thinning.short: Give individual plants room once they can be handled
thinning.guidance: Field guidance thins to about 6 inches. In a pod, translate that into avoiding a dense cluster rather than copying the soil spacing literally.

pruning.guidance: Chervil is primarily harvested for tender leaves; avoid aggressive structural pruning on a young plant.

harvest.guidance: Johnny's notes peak leaf flavor just before flowering. Use light leaf/stem harvests earlier as needed.

flowering.short: Heat-driven bolting ends the prime leaf phase
flowering.guidance: Hot weather can trigger bolting; record flowering as a stage transition and expect leaf quality to decline.

hydroponics.short: Hydro-specific nutrient targets still need validation
hydroponics.guidance: Keep chervil in the structured library, but do not assign a precise hydroponic EC range until a crop-specific source is accepted.

problems.short: Heat and dryness are the main management risks
problems.guidance: Chervil prefers rich, moist conditions and is sensitive to hot weather.

name: Garlic Chives
summary: A perennial clump-forming allium with flat leaves and edible flowers. Like common chives, it should not be forced into a one-seedling-per-pod rule.

germination.guidance: UNH Extension lists 7–14 day germination for garlic chives.

thinning.short: A clump is normal; overcrowding is the trigger
thinning.guidance: Garlic chives naturally form clumps. Garden should thin only when crowding limits airflow or light rather than aiming for a single stem.

pruning.short: Harvest leaves low and allow regrowth
pruning.guidance: Treat cutting as harvest rather than branching pruning; established allium leaves regrow from the base.

harvest.short: Young leaves are harvestable anytime after establishment
harvest.guidance: UNH Extension notes young leaves can be harvested anytime and flowers are edible shortly after opening.

flowering.short: Flowers are edible but can self-seed aggressively
flowering.guidance: White flowers are edible; deadhead before seed set when spread control matters.

hydroponics.short: Compact clumps are plausible; exact nutrient range pending
hydroponics.guidance: No crop-specific hydroponic EC/pH target is accepted in V0.5 yet.

problems.short: Overcrowding and self-seeding are the main structural risks
problems.guidance: Dense clumps benefit from periodic division in long-lived culture.

name: Evergreen Bunching Onion Nabuka
spanishName: Cebolla de verdeo Evergreen Bunching Nabuka
summary: A bunching onion / scallion type grown for repeated green stalk harvest rather than a large storage bulb. Cluster culture is normal for this crop class.

germination.guidance: Johnny's bunching-onion guidance starts 6–8 seeds per cell for transplant culture, confirming that cluster growth is intentional.

thinning.short: Do not automatically reduce to one plant
thinning.guidance: For bunching onions, thin only when the cluster becomes too dense for the target stalk size and available root volume.

pruning.guidance: Management is harvest-oriented; do not cut the center as if this were a branching herb.

harvest.short: Harvest green stalks / whole bunches by intended use
harvest.guidance: Bunching onions are harvested as scallions. In a regenerative container, selective outer-stalk cutting can be tested, but whole-plant harvest remains the canonical production method.

flowering.short: Flowering is not the culinary target
flowering.guidance: Allowing flowering shifts energy away from tender scallion production and should be treated as a stage change.

hydroponics.short: Suitable architecture for hydro, exact nutrient target pending
hydroponics.guidance: The upright, clustered growth habit is compatible with compact systems, but V0.5 does not assign a precise crop-specific EC range.

problems.guidance: Maximum light and enough root volume matter more than chasing a fixed seedling count.

name: Dwarf Bedding Petunia — Mixed Colors
spanishName: Petunia enana de macizo — mezcla de colores
summary: A compact annual ornamental selected for continuous bloom. This is primarily a container/soil crop in the current Garden library rather than a hydroponic priority.

metrics.label: Bloom
metrics.note: Online reference gives a broader range

germination.guidance: Ferry-Morse lists 7–12 day germination for Dwarf Bedding Petunia.

thinning.guidance: The manufacturer directs thinning when plants are about 2 inches high. For containers, keep enough spacing to preserve airflow and light around each crown.

pruning.short: Shape lightly if plants become leggy
pruning.guidance: V0.5 does not yet treat petunia pruning as a canonical rule; deadheading and light shaping can be recommended contextually.

harvest.short: Cut flowers are optional; display bloom is the main goal
harvest.guidance: This ornamental is primarily maintained for continuous display rather than edible harvest.

flowering.short: Continuous bloom from spring toward frost
flowering.guidance: The variety is sold for heavy, continuous flowering; spent-bloom management can be used to keep the display tidy.

hydroponics.guidance: Garden should favor container/soil guidance for this ornamental until a specific hydroponic use case exists.

problems.short: Legginess and reduced bloom under poor light
problems.guidance: Compact form depends on adequate light and balanced growth; avoid crowding behind taller crops.

name: American Giant Hybrid Sunflower
summary: A truly giant sunflower that can reach roughly 12–16 feet outdoors. It is a poor physical neighbor for low crops in tight spaces because shade and root demand dominate the decision.

thinning.short: Final spacing matters because mature size is enormous
thinning.guidance: Keep the strongest seedlings and avoid close final spacing; this variety is selected for giant stature.

pruning.guidance: Garden should not assume branching-prune logic for a giant sunflower without a specific production goal.

harvest.short: Flowers and mature seed heads are the useful endpoints
harvest.guidance: This variety is suitable for ornamental bloom and edible seed harvest after heads mature and dry.

flowering.guidance: Ferry-Morse lists strong pollinator and songbird value for the mature flowers and seed heads.

hydroponics.short: Not appropriate for a small countertop hydro system
hydroponics.guidance: The mature height, support requirement and root demand make this a soil/large-container crop for Garden planning.

problems.short: Wind, support, shade and space dominate management
problems.guidance: Place where the mature plant cannot shade shorter crops or interfere with structures.

name: Autumn Beauty Sunflower — Mixed Colors
spanishName: Girasol Autumn Beauty — mezcla de colores
summary: A multi-branching 5–6 foot sunflower mix with strong pollinator value. Still tall enough to create meaningful shade for low neighboring crops.

thinning.short: Give each final plant room to branch
thinning.guidance: Avoid dense final stands if the goal is full branching and airflow.

pruning.guidance: The manufacturer recommends removing faded flowers to prolong bloom; structural pruning is otherwise not a default V0.5 action.

harvest.short: Suitable as a cut flower and later bird/seed resource
harvest.guidance: Use flowers for cutting or leave mature heads for seed and songbirds.

flowering.short: Gold, rust, orange and red branching blooms
flowering.guidance: This variety is grown for a long multicolor flowering display and pollinator value.

hydroponics.short: Better suited to soil or a large outdoor container
hydroponics.guidance: Its 5–6 foot mature frame and branching habit make compact hydroponics a poor fit.

problems.guidance: Position intentionally so mature stems do not shade low edible crops.

name: Jolly Jester Marigold
summary: A compact ornamental marigold in the owned seed collection. Garden can already use it as a pollinator/pest-management neighbor candidate, while exact cultivar care still needs a stronger primary source.

germination.short: Exact cultivar timing still needs source validation
germination.guidance: The owned packet confirms the cultivar and bloom target, but V0.5 keeps germination specifics unresolved until a stronger cultivar source is accepted.

thinning.short: Thin for airflow and a compact crown
thinning.guidance: Keep the strongest seedlings and prevent dense final crowding in containers.

pruning.guidance: Remove spent blooms when the goal is continued display; stronger structural pruning is not canonical yet.

harvest.guidance: Primary use is bloom and pollinator habitat rather than edible harvest.

flowering.short: Useful near vulnerable vegetables in outdoor companion layouts
flowering.guidance: USU Extension includes marigolds among pest-repellent companion plants used near vulnerable vegetables, while Garden should avoid claiming every traditional pairing is proven.

hydroponics.guidance: Do not prioritize shared-reservoir hydroponics for this ornamental until there is a real use case.

problems.short: Crowding reduces airflow and bloom quality
problems.guidance: Keep enough light around the canopy and avoid burying it under taller neighbors.

name: Lilliput Zinnia — Mixed Colors
summary: A compact 16–18 inch annual zinnia with fast germination and strong pollinator value. Useful in containers and outdoor companion layouts without the extreme shade risk of giant sunflowers.

germination.guidance: Ferry-Morse lists 5–10 day germination for Lilliput Zinnia.

thinning.short: Thin once plants are a few inches tall
thinning.guidance: Manufacturer guidance explicitly thins after seedlings gain a few inches of height.

pruning.short: Deadhead faded blooms to prolong flowering
pruning.guidance: Remove faded blossoms through the season; this is the primary maintenance action in V0.5.

harvest.guidance: The variety is marketed for long-lasting cut flowers as well as bedding use.

flowering.short: Long summer color with pollinator value
flowering.guidance: Zinnia flowers attract bees, butterflies and other pollinators.

hydroponics.guidance: Use container or bed culture first; no crop-specific hydroponic target is accepted in V0.5.

problems.guidance: Avoid overcrowding; zinnias perform best when foliage has room and light.

name: Magic Fountains Dwarf Delphinium — Mixed Colors
spanishName: Delphinium Magic Fountains enano — mezcla de colores
summary: A dwarf perennial delphinium for cool-climate ornamental use. Unlike the edible crops, this plant is explicitly non-edible and should remain segregated from culinary-harvest assumptions.

germination.short: Can be slow; avoid early failure labels
germination.guidance: Delphinium seed may germinate slowly and unevenly. V0.5 keeps exact timing cautious rather than inventing a tight deadline.

thinning.short: Thin once seedlings are strong enough to compare
thinning.guidance: Retain vigorous seedlings with enough final room for crown development.

pruning.short: Flower-stem management is a later-stage task
pruning.guidance: V0.5 does not yet encode cultivar-specific post-bloom cutback rules.

harvest.short: Cut flower only — never culinary harvest
harvest.guidance: Treat all plant material as ornamental; the product listing warns not to ingest seeds or plants.

flowering.short: Dwarf perennial spikes in mixed colors
flowering.guidance: Magic Fountains produces compact flower spikes suited to smaller gardens and exposed sites.

hydroponics.guidance: Keep this ornamental outside culinary shared systems in V0.5.

problems.guidance: Do not mix ornamental/non-edible harvest logic with edible Garden recommendations.

name: Dark Green Zucchini
summary: A fast, high-yield summer squash that needs far more horizontal room than the countertop herb crops. Pollination, airflow and space are central management constraints.

metrics.label: Height
metrics.note: Spread is much larger than height suggests

germination.guidance: Ferry-Morse lists 8–10 day germination for this variety.

thinning.short: Give the final plant substantial room
thinning.guidance: Zucchini is not a multi-plant countertop crop. Keep the strongest final plant per intended growing position unless a large system is explicitly designed otherwise.

pruning.short: Do not apply tomato sucker pruning
pruning.guidance: Leaf removal should be conservative and sanitation-driven; V0.5 does not encode aggressive zucchini pruning as a routine rule.

harvest.short: Harvest young fruit frequently for quality
harvest.guidance: The owned packet targets about 50 days to harvest. Regular picking helps maintain production once fruiting begins.

flowering.guidance: Johnny's notes poor fruit development can indicate insufficient pollination; flowering should trigger a pollination-aware maintenance state.

hydroponics.short: Possible only in a large dedicated system
hydroponics.guidance: OSU lists courgette/zucchini-type crops around EC 1.8–2.4 mS/cm and pH 6.0 as a reference, but the plant's physical size makes a small shared herb system inappropriate.

problems.short: Powdery mildew, airflow and pollination are major risks
problems.guidance: Johnny's highlights powdery mildew, downy mildew, bacterial wilt and drainage/airflow as key production concerns.

name: Crimson Giant Radish
summary: A fast cool-season root crop with a 30-day packet target. Consistent moisture and prompt harvest matter more than pruning.

germination.guidance: Ferry-Morse lists 5–10 day germination for Crimson Giant.

thinning.guidance: Unlike leafy herbs, radish needs enough individual root volume to swell. Thin crowded seedlings rather than allowing multiple roots to compete in one tight position.

pruning.guidance: Do not prune radish foliage as a shaping strategy; leaf area powers root development.

harvest.short: Harvest promptly at useful root size
harvest.guidance: Johnny's warns radishes can turn pithy or tough when left too long; the owned packet targets about 30 days.

flowering.short: Bolting means the root crop has moved past its ideal phase
flowering.guidance: Heat and delayed harvest can push radish out of prime root quality and toward reproductive growth.

hydroponics.short: Root geometry is the main design constraint
hydroponics.guidance: Hydroponic culture requires enough media/root space for the swollen root. Do not treat it like a lettuce net-cup without validating physical clearance.

problems.short: Heat, dryness and delayed harvest reduce quality
problems.guidance: Johnny's notes hot, dry weather can make roots tough, pithy and overly spicy.
